description: Animated floating-robot presenter/host character for video. Every clip is a background-free (alpha) animation of the same character, separated by action so it can be cut against voiceover.

canvas.anchor: character is horizontally centred; torso is intentionally cropped by the bottom edge so the clip can sit flush on the bottom of a frame

formats.gif: Transparent GIF, 640x680. 1-bit alpha, so edges are hard/aliased. Loops forever. Use for previews, slides, web embeds, and anywhere GIF is the expected format.
formats.mov_alpha: QuickTime MOV, PNG codec, RGBA. Lossless, with a full 8-bit alpha channel and soft antialiased edges. Use this in any video editor (Premiere, After Effects, DaVinci, Final Cut) for the actual render.

note_on_formats: The GIF and the MOV are the same animation. Prefer the MOV when the output is video; the GIF cannot represent partial transparency, so its edges will look slightly jagged over busy backgrounds.
agent_selection_rules: If the host has an audible line in the scene, pick a clip with mouth_moving = true.
If the host is on screen but silent, pick a clip with mouth_moving = false (idle_neutral_loop or listening_attentive_loop).
Match the on-screen layout: if a graphic sits to the host's right, use talk_point_right_loop or present_open_palm_right_loop; if it sits to the left, use talk_point_left_loop.

Reaction clips (surprised_reaction, laugh_happy_loop, thumbs_up_approve, nod_yes_agree, shake_head_no_disagree, shrug_uncertain) are one beat of emphasis. Use one per moment, then return to a talking or idle clip. Do not chain two reactions back to back.
wave_hello_intro is only for the first appearance; wave_goodbye_outro only for the last.
Every clip is a seamless loop, so hold a clip for as long as the scene needs by repeating it.
If no rule clearly applies, fall back to talk_neutral_loop when there is speech and idle_neutral_loop when there is not.

clips.title: Wave hello — intro
clips.use_when: The opening shot of a video, or the host's first appearance in a scene. Greeting only — do not use mid-explanation.

clips.title: Talking — neutral
clips.use_when: Default narration. The workhorse clip for most voiceover lines with no specific emotion or gesture needed.

clips.title: Talking — emphatic
clips.use_when: Stressed or high-energy lines: a strong claim, a punchline, a warning, or the key takeaway. Bigger movement and a brighter antenna.

clips.title: Talking — one hand raised
clips.use_when: Making a point while speaking, or gesturing toward something high on screen. Good generic 'explaining' shot with visible motion.

clips.title: Talking — explaining with both hands
clips.use_when: Walking through a concept, a list, or a comparison. The most 'teacher-like' talking shot; good for longer explanatory passages.

clips.title: Talking — pointing screen-right
clips.use_when: A graphic, chart, lower-third or text appears on the RIGHT side of the frame and the host is referring to it.

clips.title: Talking — pointing screen-left
clips.use_when: A graphic, chart, lower-third or text appears on the LEFT side of the frame and the host is referring to it.

clips.title: Presenting — open palm to screen-right
clips.use_when: Introducing or 'handing off' to something on the right: a product shot, a chart reveal, a guest, or the next section.

clips.title: Point up — key point
clips.use_when: Flagging the single most important idea: 'here's the key', 'remember this', numbered step one, or a callout appearing above the host.

clips.title: Thinking — processing
clips.use_when: Posing a rhetorical question, pausing before an answer, or under a line like 'so why does this happen?'. Eyes drift up and the antenna pulses like a loading indicator.

clips.title: Idle — neutral
clips.use_when: Default resting shot. Use between lines, under B-roll, on a title card, or any time the host is on screen but not speaking.

clips.title: Listening — attentive
clips.use_when: The host is reacting to someone else's audio, a quote, a guest clip, or an on-screen graphic. Small agreeable nods, mouth closed.

clips.title: Nod — yes / agree
clips.use_when: Confirming a statement, answering yes, or acknowledging a point. Two clear nods, returns to rest.

clips.title: Head shake — no / disagree
clips.use_when: Negating a myth, correcting a misconception, or answering no. Pair with lines like 'not quite' or 'that's a myth'.

clips.title: Thumbs up — approve
clips.use_when: Endorsing a tip, marking a 'do this' item, or a positive verdict in a review. Reads as approval without dialogue.

clips.title: Shrug — uncertain / it depends
clips.use_when: 'It depends', 'nobody really knows', or presenting a trade-off with no clear winner. Shoulders lift with the hands.

clips.title: Surprised — reaction
clips.use_when: A reveal, a shocking statistic, or a plot twist lands. Eyes snap wide and the antenna flares; use sparingly for a single beat.

clips.title: Laughing — happy
clips.use_when: After a joke, a light aside, or a fun fact. Eyes curve into happy arcs and the whole robot bounces; do not use for serious content.

clips.title: Wave goodbye — outro
clips.use_when: The closing shot: sign-off, end card, subscribe prompt. Calmer, slower wave than the intro, with a soft smile.
